items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: But when I was there it was almost a family affair because we all worked together with each other. And Scott Bagley was the only one that I could remember that dropped out

ctx.x: Yeah there were a lot of changes in that band you told him at once I mean.

Men would come and go. No not too many in that band. My band had a lot of changes but not Troy's band. They only changed, well after yes after I left he started to change a lot of musicians to try to keep the remnants going. But when I was there it was almost a family affair because we all worked together with each other. And Scott Bagley was the only one that I could remember that dropped out and got a replacement with Herschel Evans. Because Fred Murphy didn't want to leave Dallas, Texas I tried to get Fred to…
Did he play alcohol or tennis? Alton.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: And Sykai Collins played the alto solos and then there was Scott Bagby played the clarinet solos.

ctx.x: Now did you tell me what your motto was? You did, didn't you, the greatest swing band?

Oh well that was in later years Paul. You see originally my band was named Don Albert and his 10 Pals. Some said 10 Happy Pals. But I don't ever remember that I called it the Happy Pals but since they said it was that, it didn't interfere too much with the name. It's already 10 Pals. Yeah. And we were happy to be together and I said make the name all right. But in later years as I increased the band I'm the first one that used the word swing. And a lot of times it was misinterpreted. People would say what do you…
You said you knew Buddy Petit?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-29
items.q: He possibly was just coming in there, but that was Bagby playing that clarinet.

ctx.x: So it might be Herschel or it might be Scott.

Yeah, at the beginning of the solo, to remind me of Herschel, but I have always been in doubt that Herschel was in the band. He possibly was just coming in there, but that was Bagby playing that clarinet.
Oh, so you may have had Scott got back. You may have had four saxes.
